audit_metadata.paper_title: Multi-omics fusion with machine learning enables robust prediction of treatment response in ovarian cancer for precision population health

verbatim_contradicted_claims.section: Methods — Study cohort and data acquisition
verbatim_contradicted_claims.quote: After matching transcriptomic, RPPA proteomic, DNA methylation, treatment-response, and pharmaceutical-treatment information across data layers, 375 patients were retained as the matched multi-omics modeling cohort for model development and evaluation.
verbatim_contradicted_claims.empirical_contradiction: 375 = 279 + 96 double-counts 62 exact rows copied into both train and test. Deduplicating train∩test yields 313 rows, 224 unique 143-feature vectors, and 210 patient-level aliquot connected components.

verbatim_contradicted_claims.quote: To enable unbiased model evaluation, the matched multi-omics modeling cohort (n = 375) was randomly partitioned into a training set (n = 279) and an independent held-out test set (n = 96) using a fixed random seed of 42, corresponding to an approximate 74.4%/25.6% train-test split.
verbatim_contradicted_claims.empirical_contradiction: 62/96 (64.58%) of test rows are byte-for-byte identical to training rows, with 24/24 shared feature vectors exhibiting exact multiplicity parity k_train_pre == k_test and identical row ordering (p = 10^-14.84 conditional on shared vectors; 0/39 M=2 vectors split (1,1), p = 10^-8.12).

verbatim_contradicted_claims.section: Methods — Model training and hyperparameter optimization
verbatim_contradicted_claims.quote: To prevent information leakage, all imputation, scaling, feature selection, and oversampling steps were fitted exclusively within the training data. During cross-validation, oversampling was applied only to the training fold and never to validation folds or the held-out test samples.
verbatim_contradicted_claims.empirical_contradiction: Supplementary Fig. 5 learning-curve X-axes reach 328 (0.8*411), 427 (0.8*534), 443 (0.8*554), and 675 (0.8*844), proving 5-fold CV was run directly on the post-ADASYN/post-SMOTE oversampled matrices rather than applying oversampling inside folds.

verbatim_contradicted_claims.quote: The independent held-out test set contained 96 real patients, retained a 96 × 143 feature matrix, and was not oversampled.
verbatim_contradicted_claims.empirical_contradiction: The 96 test rows contain only 56 unique feature vectors (including one 12-copy clone and four 3-copy clones) and only 32 unique unseen feature vectors (34 unseen rows).

verbatim_contradicted_claims.section: Results — Learning-curve analysis further supports the generalizability of OMICS-FUSE
verbatim_contradicted_claims.quote: As the size of the training set increased, the training AUC gradually decreased while the validation AUC steadily improved, with both curves converging toward similar values.
verbatim_contradicted_claims.empirical_contradiction: In Supplementary Fig. 5a–d, the blue Training ROC-AUC curve is flat at 1.000 across every training set size in all four modalities — it never decreases.

combined_parity_summary.note: Modalities share overlapping TCGA-OV patients so cross-modality products are not statistically independent; each modality individually has p <= 10^-14.84.

caveats_and_adversarial_checks.summary: For Early Fusion (143 features), Methylation (256 features), and Transcriptome (191 features), the columns in MOESM4_ESM.xlsx were already pre-selected by LASSO (C=0.1) on the authors' leaked training data. Consequently, our Regime (d) strict 5-fold deduplicated CV across pooled unique patients is optimistically biased upward by pre-CV supervised feature selection. By contrast, Regime (c) (truly unseen unique test patients) has ZERO feature-selection leakage and ZERO patient leakage because those patients never appeared in the training matrix at all; and Proteomics (240 features) used unsupervised variance filtering rather than supervised LASSO.

MOESM4_ESM.xlsx proteomics sheets contain 240 features, whereas Methods and GitHub best_features_XGBoost_pharma_yes_proteomics.csv list 245 features (6 in GitHub missing from XLSX: ERRalpha, Lasu1, RPA32, SHP2_pY542, YAP, p38-a; 1 in XLSX missing from GitHub: Gli3). Early Fusion (143), Methylation (256), and Transcriptome (191) match GitHub 100% in exact order.

In main-text Table 2, TN and FP are transposed in all 5 Top-20 confusion matrices relative to Supplementary Fig. 1b and Table 2's own Accuracy/F1 values (e.g., RF_Top20 prints [[7,11],[3,75]] instead of [[11,7],[3,75]]). In Table 1, Proteomics XGBoost Precision (0.881) and Recall (0.965) conflict with Supplementary Fig. 3 [[54,14],[2,113]] (actual Precision=0.890, Recall=0.983) and with Table 1's own F1=0.934 (2*0.881*0.965/(0.881+0.965)=0.921).

Unseen non-responder specificity bounds must distinguish: (i) unconditional zero-assumption upper bounds min(TN, U0)/U0 (75.0% EF, 64.3% Tran, 100% Prot/Meth); (ii) monotonicity upper bounds assuming only Spec_leaked >= Spec_unseen, equal to overall specificity TN/(L0+U0) (50.0% EF, 45.0% Tran, 79.4% Prot, 72.2% Meth); and (iii) memorization-implied unseen specificity (TN - L0_unambig)/U0 under exact memorization of training clones (supported by Supp Fig 5 Training AUC = 1.000 and verified empirically on our pure-NumPy models): 25.0% (3/12) EF, 21.4% (3/14) Tran, 22.2% (4/18) Prot, and 12.5% (3/24) [or 8.3% (2/24)] Meth.

We explicitly tested the benign hypothesis that repeated vectors represent legitimate multiple clinical regimens per patient. This explanation fails on four independent grounds: (1) zero disclosure anywhere in the manuscript (which calls them '375 patients', '279 real patients', and '96 real patients'); (2) baseline pre-treatment omics X and patient-level response labels y cannot legally be split across train and test; (3) multi-aliquot Cartesian blocks (e.g., 2x2 methylation x transcriptome blocks repeated identically across splits) occur; and (4) 142/142 (100%) shared vectors across all 4 modalities have exact parity k_train_pre == k_test and identical row ordering with 0/216 M=2 vectors splitting (1,1) — mathematically impossible under random row splitting (p <= 10^-14.84 per modality) and matching an 80/20 non-unique ID split followed by .isin(train_ids)/.isin(test_ids) filtering (chi2 = 0.055–1.249, df=2, all p > 0.53).

This audit verifies the computational dataset, ML pipeline, and reported predictive metrics (Table 1, Table 2, Supplementary Figs. 1–5, MOESM4_ESM.xlsx). It makes no claim regarding the integrity of the downstream cell-line RT-qPCR/ELISA experiments (CASP8, AQP8, CAV1, FN1, CREB1, KDR), though those hub genes were prioritized downstream of SHAP on the leaked ML models.
